text:
Olen Zellweger has slotted into Buffalo's lineup like he's been there for years: nearly 20 minutes a night across 16 games since coming over from Anaheim, and the Sabres take 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five, much better than without him. Die by the Blade's verdict, "Fitting Right In", is hard to argue with.

He's a 5'10" defenceman who plays fast (97th percentile top speed by NHL Edge) and goes where defencemen usually don't. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 2.2 chances per 60 from in front of the net last season, 97th percentile, with a third of his shots coming off the rush, almost double the typical defenceman. Evolving-Hockey had him 49th of 215 defencemen in 2025-26, mostly on even-strength offence. His three goals so far run ahead of his chances, but the Sabres have been unlucky with him on the ice overall, so the points (six) should catch up. He's not on the power play yet, which is the obvious next step.
